title: Direct, Inverse and Joint Variation
short: y = kx, y = k/x and y = kxz.

blocks.html: Many formulas in science say how one quantity changes with another. Variation is the language for the simplest of these. You will rearrange formulas as in Solving for a Variable and recognize the shapes of the Parent Functions $y = x$ and $y = \frac{1}{x}$.

Direct: $y = kx$ ($y$ doubles when $x$ doubles). Inverse: $y = \frac{k}{x}$ ($y$ halves when $x$ doubles). Joint: $y = kxz$. "Inversely as the square" means $y = \frac{k}{x^2}$. In every case, use one known pair to find $k$, then use $k$ to answer the question.

Direct variation means the ratio $\frac{y}{x}$ stays fixed, so $k$ is that ratio, and the graph is a line through the origin. Inverse variation means the product $xy$ stays fixed, so $k$ is that product, and the graph is a stretched copy of $\frac{1}{x}$. Once you know $k$, the relationship is completely known.

blocks.name: graph
blocks.cap: Direct variation $f(x) = kx$ and inverse variation $g(x) = \frac{k}{x}$ with the same $k$. Change $k$: both graphs stretch.

blocks.title: Inverse variation
blocks.q: The time to drive a fixed distance varies inversely with speed. At 60 mph it takes 3 hours. How long at 45 mph?

blocks.title: Inverse square
blocks.q: Light intensity varies inversely with the square of distance. At 2 m it is 90 units. Find it at 6 m.
steps: $I = \frac{360}{36} = 10$. (Triple the distance, one ninth the light.)

blocks.title: Joint variation
blocks.q: $y$ varies jointly with $x$ and $z$, and $y = 60$ when $x = 3$ and $z = 4$. Find $y$ when $x = 5$ and $z = 2$.

blocks.html: Using the direct-variation idea for an inverse problem: "45 is less than 60, so the time is less." Ask which way the quantities move. For inverse variation the product stays the same: $60 \cdot 3 = 45 \cdot t$.
